data.scenario_text: A slice is cut from a round pizza whose radius is <m>7</m> inches. The slice is cut so that its tip, at the center of the pizza, forms an angle of <m>32^\circ</m>.
data.length_task: The crust runs along the outer arc of the slice. To the nearest inch, how many inches of crust does the slice have?
data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The slice is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 7 inches, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 32^\circ, both straight sides 7 inches, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the two cuts, and the arc is the crust.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 32^\circ = 32^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{8}{45} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 0.5585\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 7 inches and \theta \approx 0.5585 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(7\ \text{in})^2 \left(\frac{8}{45} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 13.68\ \text{in}^2

The caterer charges \$0.07 for every square inch, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square inch units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 13.68\ \text{in}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.07}{1\ \text{in}^2} = \boxed{\$0.96}

So the total cost to buy the slice is \boxed{\$0.96}.

Part (c). The arc is the curved outer edge of the slice, and its length is s = r\theta, with \theta in radians (the same value we used in part (b)).

s = r\theta = (7\ \text{in})\left(\frac{8}{45} \, \pi\right) \approx \boxed{4.0\ \text{in}}

So the slice has about 4.0 inches of crust.

data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 12 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 40^\circ, both straight sides 12 feet, and the arc s. \theta = 40^\circ = 40^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{2}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 0.6981\ \text{rad}

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(12\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{2}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 50.27\ \text{ft}^2

Part (a). The slice is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 8 inches, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 72^\circ, both straight sides 8 inches, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the two cuts, and the arc is the crust.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 72^\circ = 72^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{2}{5} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 1.2566\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 8 inches and \theta \approx 1.2566 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(8\ \text{in})^2 \left(\frac{2}{5} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 40.21\ \text{in}^2

The caterer charges \$0.14 for every square inch, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square inch units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 40.21\ \text{in}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.14}{1\ \text{in}^2} = \boxed{\$5.63}

So the total cost to buy the slice is \boxed{\$5.63}.

Part (c). The arc is the curved outer edge of the slice, and its length is s = r\theta, with \theta in radians (the same value we used in part (b)).

s = r\theta = (8\ \text{in})\left(\frac{2}{5} \, \pi\right) \approx \boxed{10.0\ \text{in}}

So the slice has about 10.0 inches of crust.

Part (a). The region cleared by the wiper is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 18 inches, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 70^\circ, both straight sides 18 inches, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the wiper arm in its starting and ending positions, and the arc is the path swept out by the tip of the blade.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 70^\circ = 70^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{7}{18} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 1.2217\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 18 inches and \theta \approx 1.2217 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(18\ \text{in})^2 \left(\frac{7}{18} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 197.92\ \text{in}^2

The auto detailer charges \$0.11 for every square inch, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square inch units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 197.92\ \text{in}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.11}{1\ \text{in}^2} = \boxed{\$21.77}

So the total cost to treat the region cleared by the wiper is \boxed{\$21.77}.

Part (c). The arc is the curved outer edge of the region cleared by the wiper, and its length is s = r\theta, with \theta in radians (the same value we used in part (b)).

s = r\theta = (18\ \text{in})\left(\frac{7}{18} \, \pi\right) \approx \boxed{22.0\ \text{in}}

So the tip of the wiper blade travels about 22.0 inches in a single sweep.

data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 16 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 55^\circ, both straight sides 16 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

Now substitute r = 16 feet and \theta \approx 0.9599 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(16\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{11}{36} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 122.87\ \text{ft}^2

The refinishing company charges \$3.70 for every square foot, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square foot units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 122.87\ \text{ft}^2 \cdot \frac{\$3.70}{1\ \text{ft}^2} = \boxed{\$454.62}

So about 47.0 feet of brass strip are needed.

Part (a). The region cleared by the wiper is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 18 inches, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 125^\circ, both straight sides 18 inches, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the wiper arm in its starting and ending positions, and the arc is the path swept out by the tip of the blade.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 125^\circ = 125^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{25}{36} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 2.1817\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 18 inches and \theta \approx 2.1817 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(18\ \text{in})^2 \left(\frac{25}{36} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 353.43\ \text{in}^2

The auto detailer charges \$0.11 for every square inch, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square inch units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 353.43\ \text{in}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.11}{1\ \text{in}^2} = \boxed{\$38.88}

So the total cost to treat the region cleared by the wiper is \boxed{\$38.88}.

Part (c). The arc is the curved outer edge of the region cleared by the wiper, and its length is s = r\theta, with \theta in radians (the same value we used in part (b)).

s = r\theta = (18\ \text{in})\left(\frac{25}{36} \, \pi\right) \approx \boxed{39.0\ \text{in}}

So the tip of the wiper blade travels about 39.0 inches in a single sweep.

data.solution_steps:
Part (a). The lit region is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 8 feet, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 80^\circ, both straight sides 8 feet, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the outer edges of the light beam, and the arc is the far edge of the lit region.

Now substitute r = 8 feet and \theta \approx 1.3963 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(8\ \text{ft})^2 \left(\frac{4}{9} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 44.68\ \text{ft}^2

So about 27.0 feet of brass strip are needed.

Part (a). The slice is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 6 inches, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 32^\circ, both straight sides 6 inches, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the two cuts, and the arc is the crust.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 32^\circ = 32^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{8}{45} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 0.5585\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 6 inches and \theta \approx 0.5585 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(6\ \text{in})^2 \left(\frac{8}{45} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 10.05\ \text{in}^2

The caterer charges \$0.11 for every square inch, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square inch units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 10.05\ \text{in}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.11}{1\ \text{in}^2} = \boxed{\$1.11}

So the total cost to buy the slice is \boxed{\$1.11}.

Part (c). The arc is the curved outer edge of the slice, and its length is s = r\theta, with \theta in radians (the same value we used in part (b)).

s = r\theta = (6\ \text{in})\left(\frac{8}{45} \, \pi\right) \approx \boxed{3.0\ \text{in}}

So the slice has about 3.0 inches of crust.

Part (a). The slice is a circular sector, the part of a circle cut off by a central angle. Sketch it by marking the vertex of the angle, drawing the two straight sides out to a length of 8 inches, and joining their far ends with the curved arc. Label the central angle 50^\circ, both straight sides 8 inches, and the arc s. For this situation the two straight sides are the two cuts, and the arc is the crust.

Part (b). The area of a sector is A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta, but that formula only works when the angle is measured in radians, so we convert the given angle first.

\theta = 50^\circ = 50^\circ \cdot \frac{\pi\ \text{rad}}{180^\circ} = \frac{5}{18} \, \pi\ \text{rad} \approx 0.8727\ \text{rad}

Now substitute r = 8 inches and \theta \approx 0.8727 radians into the area formula:

A = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \theta = \frac{1}{2}(8\ \text{in})^2 \left(\frac{5}{18} \, \pi\ \text{rad}\right) \approx 27.93\ \text{in}^2

The caterer charges \$0.13 for every square inch, so we multiply the area by that rate. The square inch units cancel, leaving dollars:

\text{cost} = 27.93\ \text{in}^2 \cdot \frac{\$0.13}{1\ \text{in}^2} = \boxed{\$3.63}

So the total cost to buy the slice is \boxed{\$3.63}.

Part (c). The arc is the curved outer edge of the slice, and its length is s = r\theta, with \theta in radians (the same value we used in part (b)).

s = r\theta = (8\ \text{in})\left(\frac{5}{18} \, \pi\right) \approx \boxed{7.0\ \text{in}}

So the slice has about 7.0 inches of crust.
